deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from pp. 1–4: A is a small category and φ: A → 𝔛 is a functor into a topos, written α ↦ U_α. Grothendieck lists 'covering' conditions on φ, presumably so that the U_α can serve as a nice covering or atlas of 𝔛 in the stratified-topos project.

- Hyp 1 / 1′: the family (U_α → e) is epimorphic.
- Hyp 2: for α, β ∈ Ob A, the family U_γ → U_α × U_β is epimorphic. It is indexed by the spans α ← γ → β, i.e. by the objects of A/(α×β), with the product taken in A^.

The page opens by finishing the induction begun on p. 2. Hyp 1′ plus binary Hyp 2 give the n-ary form for (α_0, …, α_n). The proof uses that a composite of covering families is covering, together with stability of epimorphic families under ×id in a topos.

Hyp 2′ is the relative version. For every α_0, the induced functor A/α_0 → 𝔛/U_{α_0} satisfies Hyp 2. Concretely, for each cospan α_1 → α_0 ← α_2, the commutative squares γ → α_1, α_2 over α_0 index a family U_γ → U_{α_1} ×_{U_{α_0}} U_{α_2}, and this family is required to be epimorphic.

Grothendieck then reformulates via the left Kan extension φ_!: A^ → 𝔛, the unique colimit-preserving extension along Yoneda (φ_!(F) = colim_{A/F} U_α). Using φ_!(F) = colim over the category of elements of F, the three hypotheses become, as p. 4 states:
- (a) φ_!(e) → e is epi;
- (b) φ_!(α×β) → φ_!α × φ_!β is epi;
- (c) φ_!(α ×_{α_0} β) → φ_!α ×_{φ_!α_0} φ_!β is epi.

Page 4 then notes that if φ_! is left exact, i.e. φ_! = f* for a geometric morphism f: 𝔛 → A^ (φ flat), these maps are isomorphisms. He conjectures the converse (isomorphisms imply left exactness).

Modern reading: this is the 'filtering functor' characterisation of flat functors, in its epimorphic-family form. Hyp 1, 2, 2′ are weak, 'covering' versions of flatness.
errors: No outright error. Note, however, that Hyp 1, 2, 2′ (epi versions) do not imply flatness. The standard filtering criterion (SGA 4 IV; Mac Lane–Moerdijk VII.9) needs an equalizer condition rather than the pullback condition (c).

Counterexample: take A a nontrivial group G as a one-object category, 𝔛 = Set, φ constant 1, so φ_! is 'orbits'. Then (a) and (c) are isomorphisms and (b) is epi, yet φ_! is not left exact. Grothendieck only calls the left-exact case 'particulièrement agréable' (p. 4), so he does not claim equivalence; the page is consistent.

When A is a preorder, equalizers are trivial. Then Hyp 1 + Hyp 2 already imply flatness, so Hyp 2′ is redundant and all the maps are even isomorphisms. His introducing Hyp 2′ separately suggests he has non-posetal A in mind.

ideas.what: n-ary covering condition follows from nullary plus binary, by induction using composites of covering families
ideas.modern_name: finite-product form of the filtering condition
ideas.where_published: close to SGA 4 Exp. IV §4.9 discussion of flat/filtering functors

ideas.what: Relative (sliced) covering condition on fibre products U_{α1} ×_{U_{α0}} U_{α2}
ideas.modern_name: covering-flat / pullback-filtering condition for a functor into a topos
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 IV (flat functors); later literature on covering-flat functors

ideas.what: Reformulation of the hypotheses as epimorphy of comparison maps for φ_!, the colimit-preserving extension to presheaves
ideas.modern_name: flat functor / left Kan extension and Diaconescu's theorem

deep.surprise_reason: Standard flat/filtering-functor material from SGA 4, reformulated in epimorphic-family form as preliminary set-up for stratified topoi. Nothing beyond the literature.

𝔛_{/α_0} denotes 𝔛 sliced over U_{α_0}.
